graph.summary: Empagliflozin → Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 → renal glucose absorption → Hyperglycemia → Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2

evidence.snippet: Empagliflozin is a selective SGLT2 inhibitor that works by constraining glucose reabsorption in the kidneys, causing increased urinary glucose elimination.
evidence.explanation: Pharmacological review confirming empagliflozin selectively inhibits SGLT2 activity, constraining its renal glucose reabsorption function.

paper.title: Empagliflozin-A Sodium Glucose Co-transporter-2 Inhibitor: Overview ofits Chemistry, Pharmacology, and Toxicology.

evidence.snippet: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) acts as a key element in the reabsorption of glucose in the kidney.
evidence.explanation: SGLT2 is the key transporter driving renal glucose reabsorption; it positively regulates this biological process.

paper.title: The effects of empagliflozin in patients with type 1 diabetes: Results of a 12-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

evidence.snippet: work by blocking SGLT2 proteins in the proximal convoluted tubules of the nephrons, thereby preventing glucose reabsorption into the bloodstream.
evidence.explanation: Blocking SGLT2 prevents renal glucose reabsorption, confirming that SGLT2 positively regulates this process.

paper.title: The Effects of Sodium-Glucose Co-transporter 2 Inhibitors on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.snippet: SGLT2 inhibitors are a class of oral antidiabetic drugs that lower elevated plasma glucose levels by promoting the urinary excretion of excess glucose through the inhibition of renal glucose reuptake.
evidence.explanation: Inhibiting renal glucose reabsorption lowers plasma glucose, establishing that renal glucose reabsorption is positively correlated with blood glucose / hyperglycemia.

paper.title: Mechanistic evaluation of the effect of sodium-dependent glucose transporter 2 inhibitors on delayed glucose absorption in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus using a quantitative systems pharmacology model of human systemic glucose dynamics.

evidence.snippet: Ipragliflozin significantly lowered blood glucose levels in mice that had prefasted for 0, 6, or 12 h, but not 18 h or more.
evidence.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated reduction of renal glucose reabsorption lowers blood glucose in a blood glucose-dependent manner, supporting positive correlation between renal glucose absorption and hyperglycemia.

paper.title: SGLT2 inhibitor ipragliflozin exerts antihyperglycemic effects via the blood glucose-dependent increase in urinary glucose excretion in type 2 diabetic mice.

evidence.snippet: Diabetes mellitus is a group of diseases associated with various metabolic disorders, the main feature of which is chronic hyperglycemia due to insufficient insulin action.
evidence.explanation: Chronic hyperglycemia is the main feature (manifestation) of diabetes mellitus, including type 2 diabetes mellitus.

paper.title: Report of the committee on the classification and diagnostic criteria of diabetes mellitus.
authors: Committee of the Japan Diabetes Society on the Diagnostic Criteria of Diabetes Mellitus
